title: Accuracy of the output hypothesis
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $a\in[0,1/2]\cap\mathbb{Q}$, and let the learner's output be either absent or a decision tree on the $n$ binary coordinates with values in $\{−1,1\}$. If the output is not bad—that is, it is present and its tree computes $f$ on every input—then the hypothesis obtained from the output has relative Hamming distance at most $a$ from $f$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Optional decision tree with sign-valued leaves
Output is not bad, hence present and computes the target
